project.name: Downpress
project.description: Git-native Markdown blog engine (SvelteKit): posts are Markdown+YAML files edited directly in a GitHub repo (e.g. via the GitHub mobile app), compiled to a static prerendered site with auto-deploy on push. Structured as a reusable core engine plus independently deployable, scaffoldable sites.

decisions.decision: Use gray-matter + remark/rehype (data-driven) instead of mdsvex-as-routes for content parsing/rendering.
decisions.rationale: Posts are pure content, not interactive Svelte templates; avoids mdsvex's known limitation where a +layout.svelte can't directly read a child .md file's frontmatter; keeps frontmatter access uniform everywhere (listings, post pages, RSS, sitemap) via one loader function.

decisions.decision: Static prerendering via adapter-static, not SSR.
decisions.rationale: No runtime backend needed; output is a plain static folder deployable anywhere. Tag/pagination routes must stay crawlable or be listed explicitly in config.kit.prerender.entries.

decisions.decision: Core/site split (Downpress core engine + independent Site repos) is a first-class requirement from the start, not a later refactor.
decisions.rationale: SvelteKit's routing/build system is inherently per-project (hard framework constraint) — every Site must be its own SvelteKit project. Core centralizes content loader, markdown pipeline, feed/sitemap generators, shared layout/theme components, and scaffolding.
alternatives_considered: Single monolithic project serving multiple blogs via config (not possible under SvelteKit)

decisions.decision: Sites depend on Downpress core via a pinned git URL dependency (tag/commit), not a main-floating or npm-published dependency.
decisions.rationale: Avoids needing to publish/maintain a public npm package while still allowing normal package-manager installs; pinning means a core change never silently changes a site's next build without a deliberate version bump.
alternatives_considered: Publish core to npm under a scoped name (deferred, not needed for v1)

decisions.decision: Deploy to Cloudflare Pages, always on a custom domain from day one.
decisions.rationale: CF Pages has native git integration to build adapter-static output on push to main. A custom domain means the site is served at root, so adapter-static needs no base-path/subpath configuration.
alternatives_considered: GitHub Pages (would need base-path config unless on a custom domain)

decisions.decision: Post content lives in a top-level /posts/ directory, outside src/.
decisions.rationale: Easier to find and edit via the GitHub mobile app's file browser since it is not nested inside app source.

decisions.decision: Drafts (draft: true) are excluded from index, tag pages, RSS, and sitemap, but still built at their normal /posts/<slug> URL (unlinked) for private preview.
decisions.rationale: Lets the owner preview formatting on a phone before flipping draft: false, without exposing the post in any discoverable listing or feed.
alternatives_considered: Fully exclude drafts from build output entirely

decisions.decision: Dates are strict YYYY-MM-DD only; future-dated posts are hidden until their date arrives.
decisions.rationale: One accepted date format keeps sorting unambiguous and lets malformed dates fail loudly (naming the file). Future-dating uses a build-time 'date <= today' check tied to the CI run's date so scheduled posts stay hidden until the next build on/after that date.

decisions.decision: Visual direction is sparse, sharp/classic, high-end and uncluttered; core supports selectable per-site themes that are all variations on this shared aesthetic.
decisions.rationale: Restrained editorial typography and minimal chrome fit a text-first blog and keep client JS minimal (Lighthouse 95+ goal). Selectable themes give per-site variety without each site diverging into a wholly different design, so most theme code stays in core.
alternatives_considered: One fixed shared theme with no per-site selection

decisions.decision: Core versioning is informal (pin sites to core commit SHAs as needed); the scaffold command is a local script run from the core repo, not a published CLI.
decisions.rationale: Fastest path for v1 with a single maintainer and no public distribution; a semver release process and an npx CLI can be added later if multiple sites make change-tracking painful.
alternatives_considered: Semver-tagged core releases from the start

decisions.decision: Default theme is 'Essay' — a quiet, text-first editorial look (Ben Evans / Stratechery family) with self-hosted Newsreader (reading serif) + Inter (UI/meta), a single accent used at three intensities (strong / rule / wash), and warm parchment neutrals with a dark variant.
decisions.rationale: example-site.example is an essay site; the quiet single-column serif look serves reading and keeps client JS ~zero (Lighthouse 95+ goal, D9). Fonts are bundled via @fontsource-variable so there are no third-party font requests. Design is expressed as CSS custom properties so per-site theme variants (D9) stay cheap.

decisions.decision: First feature batch: excerpt post cards, featured latest post + index pagination (/page/[n]), optional per-post author byline, prev/next post links, a config-driven Topics/Explore view, a config-driven external newsletter CTA, and image-only paragraphs becoming <figure>+<figcaption>. Deferred: client-side search, reading-time, manual dark toggle.
decisions.rationale: Distilled from reference blogs the user shared; all are static-friendly (zero or trivial JS) and fit 'keep it simple'. Newsletter is just a link to an external service (Buttondown/Substack) — no backend, consistent with comments being a non-goal.
alternatives_considered: Include client-side search now (needs JS + build index)

gotchas.gotcha: This Svelte tooling version (Kit 2.69 / Vite 8 / vite-plugin-svelte 7) has NO svelte.config.js — adapter and kit options (adapter, prerender, compilerOptions) are passed directly to the sveltekit() plugin inside vite.config.ts.
gotchas.resolution: Configure adapter-static and prerender.entries in vite.config.ts, not a separate svelte.config.js.

gotchas.gotcha: Reading content via Node fs makes the loader server-only. If imported from a universal +page.ts it would be bundled for the client and break.
gotchas.resolution: posts.ts uses $env/dynamic/private + node:fs (server-only by construction); content routes are +page.server.ts. Pure logic is isolated in parse.ts for safe importing/testing. Requires @types/node for svelte-check.

gotchas.gotcha: sv create refuses/hangs on a non-empty directory (the repo already had docs/, .forgekit/, etc.).
gotchas.resolution: Scaffold into a fresh temp dir with fully non-interactive flags, then move files to the repo root.

gotchas.gotcha: A prerendered dynamic route with an entries() that returns [] (e.g. /page/[n] on a site small enough to fit on page 1) fails the adapter-static build with 'marked as prerenderable but not prerendered'.
gotchas.resolution: Set kit.prerender.handleUnseenRoutes in vite.config.ts to a function that ignores exactly '/page/[n]' and still throws for any other unseen route, so the build stays strict elsewhere.

sessions.summary: Ran ForgeKit greenfield kickoff for Downpress. Project already had a full GENESIS.md build spec, so it was ingested via ingestPlanArtifact and used to draft docs/PHASE_1_BRIEF.md directly (status: draft) instead of starting Phase 1 intake from scratch. Recorded D1-D4 architectural decisions from the spec's own recommendations. Brief cannot be locked yet: 11 open questions from GENESIS.md Section 9 still need explicit user answers (drafts handling, deploy target, content dir location, date format, future-dated posts, styling, comments scope, custom domain, theme sharing, core versioning, scaffold CLI distribution).

User resolved all 11 open questions. Locked docs/PHASE_1_BRIEF.md and added decisions D5-D10 (Cloudflare Pages + custom domain; top-level /posts/; hidden-URL draft preview; strict YYYY-MM-DD + hide future-dated; sparse/classic styling with selectable per-site themes; informal versioning + local scaffold script; comments a permanent non-goal). Phase 1 exit criteria all met. Held at currentPhase 1-architecture pending explicit user go-ahead to start Phase 2 scaffolding.

Phase 2 scaffolding: ran lessons gate (getAntiPatterns + searchLessons), advanced to 2-scaffolding, and built the full runnable spine in one pass. SvelteKit adapter-static app (TS/pnpm) with a complete content engine (gray-matter + remark/rehype, all edge cases, loud file-named ContentError), index/post/tag routes, RSS/sitemap/robots, and the Classic theme. Verified build + preview: drafts previewable-but-unlisted, future-dated hidden (404), dedupe + missing-field failures loud; pnpm check clean. Wrote Phase 2 docs (CONTEXT_PROMPT merged from brief, README, TODO, .forgekit/IDEAS). All Phase 2 exit criteria met; awaiting confirmation to advance to Phase 3.

Early hardening + first real site. Extracted pure parse/validate logic into src/lib/content/parse.ts; added Vitest (20 unit tests: slugify, tag normalization, strict/impossible dates, missing fields, dedupe) + @types/node. Reworked content loading to read the filesystem from DOWNPRESS_CONTENT_DIR (default posts/) instead of import.meta.glob, and made site identity env-driven (PUBLIC_SITE_*); content routes moved to +page.server.ts (loader is now server-only) — this is the seam the M4 core/site split will use. Validated end to end by building and running the engine locally as example-site.example against ../example-site/artifacts (added frontmatter to that article in place); article, tags, RSS, sitemap all correct. pnpm check + test clean. The .env and site content are gitignored/external — only engine hardening was committed. currentPhase left at 2-scaffolding pending confirmation to formally enter Phase 3.

Stage 1 of the 'A' track: feature batch + Essay restyle before the M4 core/site split (chose to add features to a stable engine first, then extract). Distilled UX from user-provided blogs (Ben Evans, Stratechery, Traveling Mitch, Copyblogger). Added (D11/D12): quiet Essay theme with self-hosted Newsreader+Inter via @fontsource-variable, three-tier accent + warm neutrals; optional author byline (parse.ts + tests, now 26 tests); excerpt post cards + featured hero; index pagination via /page/[n] (+ handleUnseenRoutes gotcha fix); prev/next post links; config-driven Topics/Explore view; config-driven external newsletter CTA; rehype-figure (image-only paragraphs -> figure+figcaption, with its own tests). Extended SiteConfig (tagline, postsPerPage, topics, newsletter) + .env.example; sitemap now lists /topics and paginated pages; README documents author + captions. pnpm check clean, 26 tests pass, adapter-static build succeeds; verified visually by previewing the example-site.example build. Next: Stage 2 = the M4 core/site split + scaffold script, then promote example-site.example to a real Site repo. currentPhase still 2-scaffolding — this is Phase-4-shaped work; awaiting user OK to flip currentPhase to 4-feature-iteration.

Stage 2 (M4 core/site split) DONE, as a pnpm workspace monorepo (user chose monorepo + confirmed flipping currentPhase to 4-feature-iteration). Extracted the whole engine into @downpress/core (packages/core, source-linked Svelte lib): content loader, remark/rehype pipeline (incl. rehype-figure), feed/sitemap/robots builders, format, Essay theme (styles/theme.css + font imports via @downpress/core/theme), and prop-driven components (PostCard, PostIndex, Newsletter, SiteHeader, SiteFooter). Redesigned for DI to remove SvelteKit-only deps ($env/$lib): createContent({contentDir}) factory (server-only), defineDownpressConfig() that validates title/url + fills defaults, and a strict client-barrel (index.ts) vs server-barrel (server.ts) split. Rebuilt the app as sites/example-site (real site; example-post.md; own downpress.config.ts + content.server.ts + thin routes). Wrote scripts/create-site.mjs (templates from example-site, refuses non-empty dir, edge case 18) and used it to generate sites/demo, then restored the original demo posts (drafts + future-dated) into it. Deleted the old root SvelteKit app; root package.json is now a workspace manifest with pnpm -r scripts. Verification: @downpress/core tests = 31 pass (added config.test.ts covering defineDownpressConfig validation, edge case 19); pnpm -r check = 0 errors; example-site and demo each build cleanly and independently to their own build/ (isolation proven). Deferred (until a second repo is actually needed, D4): splitting core into its own git repo with URL+SHA pins + a CI workflow template in the scaffold. Next milestone: M3 (Cloudflare Pages deploy wiring, per site).
